business_problem: BASF was receiving more than 500,000 supplier invoice inquiries each year through hundreds of email boxes and phone calls, leaving multiple departments with manual work, inconsistent responses, and almost no visibility into supplier-service performance.
solution_summary: BASF reworked supplier management around a global self-service model built on ServiceNow Customer Service Management. The new supplier invoice system gives suppliers secure access to live invoice status and payment dates pulled from BASF's ERP environment, so simple questions no longer require agent intervention. A multilingual knowledgebase answers common invoicing questions directly in the portal, while follow-up questions become tickets that are coded to the right recipients. ServiceNow Agent Workspace with AI then brings a supplier's full history onto one screen for agents handling exceptions, and Performance Analytics measures usage patterns and case performance so BASF can continuously refine the workflow. The architecture replaced decentralized hubs across three continents with a single digital portal that scales across more than 80,000 suppliers and sets the pattern for broader procurement-service transformation on the ServiceNow AI Platform.

data_flow: Suppliers log into BASF's portal to view live invoice and payment information from the ERP system or to search the multilingual knowledgebase. When self-service is not enough, Customer Service Management creates a ticket, routes it to the right BASF team, and surfaces full supplier context in Agent Workspace while Performance Analytics measures response behavior and portal adoption.
business_outcome: BASF cut supplier invoice inquiries from more than 500,000 to fewer than 200,000, reduced total tickets by 60%, resolved cases 50% faster, and improved end-to-end inquiry efficiency by 10% while giving suppliers faster status visibility and self-service access.
